acceptanceCriteria: A numbered spec amendment records the chosen design (lease table or seal-time coalescing), its failure modes, rollback and the hash-chain verification rule; existing stores still verify and read unchanged.

At the issue's workload shape, a measured fixture shows journal growth proportional to ownership changes, not to wall-clock x live attempts, with heartbeat/renew fencing semantics (generation, STALE_HOLDER, lease expiry) preserved by regression tests.
receipt audit and archive verify pass on a migrated or coalesced store; no history that carries ownership or outcome information is dropped.
GitHub #982 is closed by the merged PR.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#982 (2026-10-16). One real queue over 18 days: heartbeat 16,925 receipts/172 MB, renew 9,249/88 MB, of 627 MB total store; 61% of receipts and 67% of receipt bytes are liveness, each with its own request file. No retention/compaction/prune path exists; hand deletion breaks the hash chain (JOURNAL_FORKED). Complete audits replay from receipt 1, so lock hold and LOCK_TIMEOUT scale with journal size (#967 / V1-1494). Related: V1-0887 (heartbeats and renews must cost O(1), GitHub #642). Proposed options in the issue: (1) liveness in a fenced lease table outside the audited journal; (2) coalesce superseded liveness on segment seal with a verifiable dropped-range hash; (3) retention policy with default unchanged; (4) drop per-receipt request copies for liveness verbs after commit. Sequence after V1-1494 (same packages).
title: corvint-tasks: liveness receipts (heartbeat/renew) are retained forever though superseded, ~2/3 of journal bytes (GitHub #982)
